output.metric: Signups fell after a price change
output.observed_change: Signups fell 24 percent the week after a pricing page update and have not recovered.
output.notes: An unrelated schema migration ran the same week. One collector logged a transient warning.

marts.signups has NO schema fields recorded in DataHub (datahub.schema returned 0 fields) — column-level structure of the metric table is invisible.

raw.web_sessions has NO upstream lineage recorded (0 upstreams) — its producer is not captured; its description notes an is_automated flag that 'not every producer sets', so bot/automated-traffic filtering completeness cannot be verified from metadata.

channel_ingest_job is a per-channel collector where 'a dead task produces silence, not an error' — a silently dead channel would NOT raise an incident, so health=PASS across the chain does not rule out a dropped channel feeding the 24% signup fall.

Case notes mention a schema migration the same week and a transient collector warning; NEITHER is reflected in any node's DataHub metadata (all health = INCIDENTS PASS) — absence of an incident here is a coverage gap, not evidence the migration/warning was harmless.
No dbt tests/assertions surfaced for any node — only INCIDENTS health is available; assertion coverage of this lineage is itself thin.

Metric computation lives in warehouse view SQL (signups is a view; staging.events_daily 'buckets on local time', events_weekly_rollup exists) — a bucketing/filtering/definition change inside the view text would be invisible to DataHub lineage and was not read at this node; hand off to the test node.
No last_changed timestamps were available for any upstream node — cannot confirm from metadata which upstream (if any) changed during the day-1→day-36 window.

output.statement: The 24% signup drop reflects a genuine change in customer behaviour caused by the pricing page update — prospective users who saw the new price/positioning chose not to sign up — and marts.signups is correctly counting a real decline, not an artifact of the measurement path.
would_be_confirmed_by: Pricing-page funnel data show the view→signup conversion rate fell in lockstep with the metric, with the drop localized to the step after users saw the new price.
The decline is broad-based across acquisition channels rather than concentrated in one source.
Independent, path-disjoint demand signals (checkout attempts, payment intents, account-creation emails) fell by a comparable proportion over the same window.
The pricing update genuinely changed price or offer, and elasticity/benchmark estimates predict a drop of roughly this magnitude.
would_be_refuted_by: The signup decline started before the pricing page went live, breaking the causal timing.
Pricing-page view→signup conversion rate is unchanged across the change, with the drop appearing only in downstream counted rows (points to instrument/data, not behaviour).
The drop is concentrated in a single acquisition channel or single event source (e.g. one channel_ingest_job task) rather than spread across demand as a real behavioural shift would be.
Independent demand signals (checkout attempts, payment intents, support inquiries) held steady while only the warehouse signups metric fell.
The pricing 'update' was copy-only and did not change price or offer, yet signups still fell — undercutting the behavioural mechanism.
The schema migration or a collector gap that week coincides with the drop, and correcting/backfilling it restores signups to prior levels without any customer-facing change.

would_be_confirmed_by: Exactly one channel (or a table touched by the schema migration) drops to ~zero or steps down at the migration date while other channels stay flat, and its missing volume accounts for roughly the 24% gap.

raw.channel_events_raw shows a row-count step-down whose timestamp matches the schema migration or the transient collector warning, and the deficit persists (has not recovered) in lockstep with the signup metric.
channel_ingest_job run history reveals a per-channel task that has emitted zero rows since the change date without raising an incident.
would_be_refuted_by: A per-channel daily time series of raw.channel_events_raw across the window shows every channel continuous — none drops to zero or steps down around the pricing-change/migration date.

Row/event counts in raw.channel_events_raw and staging.events_daily show no discontinuity coinciding with the schema-migration date; total upstream volume is stable while only the downstream signup count fell.
channel_ingest_job run history shows every per-channel task succeeded with non-zero output for every day in day-1→day-36 (no silent dead task).
An independent signup source that does not depend on channel_ingest_job (e.g., the auth/registration system's own ledger, or web_sessions conversions) reproduces the same ~24% decline within noise.
The decline is spread proportionally across all channels and segments rather than concentrated in one channel going dark.

output.statement: The 24% signup drop is a measurement-path artifact, not fewer customers: qualifying signup events did land in raw.channel_events_raw during the day-1→day-36 window, but an unintended change in the transformation path — plausibly the same-week schema migration silently breaking a join/filter key used by staging.events_daily or the marts.signups view, or a local-time (DST/tz) bucketing shift that moved events across day/week boundaries, or the transient collector warning dropping rows — caused those present rows to be under-counted downstream, so marts.signups miscounts events it correctly received.
would_be_confirmed_by: A raw-level COUNT of qualifying signup events in raw.channel_events_raw over the window shows no drop (or a far smaller one) than marts.signups, localizing the loss to the raw→mart transformation path rather than to real events.

The schema-migration DDL is shown to have altered a column, type, or join/filter key that staging.events_daily or the marts.signups view depends on, and patching/reverting that logic restores the counts.
Events near day/week boundaries are misbucketed because staging buckets on local time, and re-bucketing on UTC removes the 24% drop.
The collector's transient warning is tied to a measurable gap in row counts through that collector during the window.
would_be_refuted_by: A row-level reconciliation shows the count of qualifying signup events present in raw.channel_events_raw matches (within noise) the count in marts.signups — no rows are lost between raw and the mart.

A naive raw-level count of signup events that bypasses the staging/mart transformations already exhibits the full 24% drop, showing the decline exists upstream of the path (pointing to input loss or real behavior, not the instrument).

Diffing the schema-migration DDL against the staging model and marts.signups view SQL shows no overlap in any column, type, join key, or filter, and no DST/timezone/bucketing boundary falls inside the window.
The collector's transient warning is shown to have dropped zero rows (continuous before/after row counts through that collector).
Re-running the unchanged view logic against a pre-migration snapshot of the raw schema still reproduces the 24% drop.

output.claim: The signups metric is a pure pass-through row count of raw.channel_events_raw with no filter, join, or bot/is_automated exclusion: signups = events_daily = COUNT(*) of channel_events_raw grouped by date(occurred_at) and channel.
output.observation: signups view DDL: CREATE VIEW signups AS SELECT bucket_date AS day, channel, events AS signups FROM events_daily. events_daily view DDL: CREATE VIEW events_daily AS SELECT date(occurred_at) AS bucket_date, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_date, channel. The only transformation from raw to metric is date() bucketing + COUNT(*); there is no WHERE filter, no join, and no is_automated/bot exclusion.

output.claim: All four acquisition channels are present in raw.channel_events_raw across the entire day-1→day-36 window; none dropped to zero or went dark.

It targets the orders table, not channel_events_raw / events_daily / signups, and only creates an index (no column drop, type change, or join/filter-key change that could silently kill a channel ingest task).

output.claim: marts.signups is a pass-through of events_daily, which is COUNT(*) of channel_events_raw grouped by date and channel with no signup-specific filter and no pricing-page or funnel input, so the metric cannot observe pricing-page viewing behavior and a fall in it is equally consistent with fewer rows landing.
output.observation: signups DDL: CREATE VIEW signups AS SELECT bucket_date AS day, channel, events AS signups FROM events_daily. events_daily DDL: CREATE VIEW events_daily AS SELECT date(occurred_at) AS bucket_date, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_date, channel. There is no WHERE clause selecting a signup event type and no join to any pricing/funnel table; 'signups' is a raw row count. The metric therefore evidences 'rows present in channel_events_raw', not 'prospective users who saw the new price and declined'.

output.narrative: marts.signups is a pure pass-through COUNT(*) of raw.channel_events_raw with no signup-type filter, join, or pricing/funnel input (e4, e11), so the metric only evidences 'rows present in raw', not prospective users reacting to a price. A per-week reconciliation shows the raw count equals the mart count exactly (593/538/608/683/732) with zero rows lost or misbucketed between raw and the mart (e25) — the measurement path is behaving as designed, so the deficit lives in the inputs, not the transformation. The shortfall is channel-concentrated: organic (133→74) and referral (156→115) fall for the Jun 9–15 week while affiliate and paid_social simultaneously rise (e2), and in raw.channel_events_raw those same two channels have absent days (organic 2026-06-10, referral 2026-06-13) and near-zero days (organic Jun-08=6, Jun-09=6, Jun-15=3 vs ~20 baseline) that snap back to baseline, while affiliate and paid_social keep a continuous non-zero row every day (e3). Independently, weekly web_sessions stayed flat for every channel (organic 428→405, −5%) even as organic signups fell −44% (e1), so top-of-funnel demand did not fall — the two paths diverge, a collection signature rather than a behavioural one. channel_ingest_job's job-level run log looks healthy (e14), but aggregate job health (min 59 rows/day across all channels) is blind to a single per-channel task going silent on a given day; the missing organic/referral channel-days in raw are that silence. A per-channel collector intermittently emitted no events for organic and referral on specific days, feeding incomplete inputs into a correct measurement path.

alternatives_rejected.hypothesis: customer_behavior (h1): the pricing page update caused a genuine, broad-based signup decline.
instrument_failure (h3): a transformation bug, broken join/filter, or local-time/DST bucketing under-counted events that were actually present in raw.

steps.action: Confirm at source before mutating anything: pull the per-channel task logs and source-of-truth event volumes for channel_ingest_job on the specific silent/near-zero days.
steps.rationale: Job-level health is green (36/36 runs, min 59 rows/day) only because that floor is summed across all four channels and is structurally blind to one channel emitting zero on a day (e14); organic's missing 2026-06-10 and near-zero Jun-08/09/15 and referral's missing 2026-06-13 in raw (e3) are that per-channel silence. Verdict confidence is 0.62 and the dip recovered on its own, so gate the corrective write on logs proving the events existed but failed to land — do not assume.

steps.action: Only if step 1 confirms lost events: re-ingest them idempotently (keyed on event_id) for the affected organic/referral days into raw.channel_events_raw.
steps.rationale: marts.signups is a pure pass-through COUNT(*) view whose weekly totals equal the raw row count week-for-week (e21, e22, e25), so restoring the missing raw rows is the single corrective write that propagates to the metric — no transformation change is warranted or safe. event_id is a stable key (e23), making the re-ingest idempotent and the inserted rows individually identifiable for rollback.

steps.action: Add a per-channel daily volume/freshness assertion on raw.channel_events_raw and a per-task check on channel_ingest_job that alerts when any single channel emits zero (or falls below a floor) for a day.
steps.rationale: The failure was invisible because 'a dead task produces silence, not an error' and no per-channel assertion exists; only an all-channel aggregate floor is watched (e14). A per-channel floor is what would have caught organic/referral going dark without raising an incident (e3), and it prevents recurrence rather than only repairing this instance.

steps.action: Assign an accountable owner to marts.signups in DataHub.
steps.rationale: marts.signups has an empty ownership record — no human was accountable to notice or triage a channel-concentrated dip. Ownership is a prerequisite for the step-3 assertion to route to someone; without it the new alert has no addressee.

steps.action: Flag for definitional review (hand off, not a corrective write): marts.signups counts every raw row via COUNT(*) with no signup-type filter, no join, and no is_automated/bot exclusion, so the metric name overstates what it measures.
steps.rationale: signups = events_daily = COUNT(*) of channel_events_raw grouped by day and channel (e4, e11). The metric evidences 'rows present in raw', not 'prospective users who signed up', and cannot on its own confirm a behavioural change or exclude bot traffic. This mislabel is why a collection gap masqueraded as a pricing-driven signup drop; the metric owner should decide whether to rename it or add a real signup filter.

output.verification: Reversible because the backfill is an idempotent re-ingest keyed on event_id, tagged with a batch id so the inserted rows can be deleted to revert; steps 3-5 (assertion, ownership, definitional flag) are trivially reversible. After backfill a human checks (a) raw.channel_events_raw now has a non-zero organic row on 2026-06-10 and referral row on 2026-06-13 and organic Jun-08/09/15 returns toward the ~20/day baseline (e3); (b) marts.signups organic/referral for that week rise toward the neighbouring-week level; (c) marts.signup_conversion_daily is re-checked — web_sessions (the denominator) was already flat (e1), so the ratio should move only via the restored numerator; (d) the new per-channel assertion fires against a synthetic zero-volume day.
